script: A newspaper sells bat men as morning truth in 1835 New York. Richard Adams Locke works in the Sun’s busy office. Rival papers stack on the wall. How do you sell the Moon for a penny? A small science column sits unsold. Richard Adams Locke types Sir John Herschel and a journal note. A page reads Great Moon Discoveries. Pennies trade for papers in seconds. An engraving shows winged Vespertilio-homo. Another plate shows tall crystal domes. A third shows a shore and herds. A rival marks a note: that journal ended 1832. Herschel maps stars far away, unaware. Front pages read August 25 to 31, 1835. A small notice hints it was fiction. Presses spin and coins fall into a box. Locke watches the stand empty fast. He sold a look. A newspaper sold the Moon for a penny.
